item.case_name: A one-minute explainer with a fixed sequence of facts: the citric acid cycle
item.title: Citric acid cycle, a 60 s explainer

turns.text: Make a 60-second widescreen explainer video on the citric acid cycle (the Krebs cycle) for first-year biology students. Show the cycle as a loop inside a mitochondrion: acetyl-CoA enters and joins oxaloacetate to form citrate, two carbons leave as CO2, NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced along the way, and oxaloacetate is regenerated so the loop starts again. Label the key molecules on screen as they appear, under the title 'Citric acid cycle'. Calm English narration explaining each step as it happens. Simple clean 2D animation, no music.

item.tests: Tests a one-minute explainer with a fixed order of facts: whether the system keeps one consistent diagram across a minute, letters short labels correctly, narrates the steps in order, and stays within the length.

must_haves: The cycle is shown as a loop, as a simple clean 2D animation inside a mitochondrion, not live action.
The steps appear in order: acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to form citrate; two carbons leave as CO2; NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced; oxaloacetate is regenerated.
Calm English narration is audible and explains each step as it happens.
The key molecules are labelled on screen as they appear, and the title 'Citric acid cycle' is shown.

stages.text:
Citric acid cycle
kind: explainer
style: 60-second widescreen explainer in simple, clean 2D animation using textbook-style diagrams; calm English narration; no music.
Under “Citric acid cycle,” an oval mitochondrial cutaway shows a symbolic, arrow-linked loop in the matrix. Labels identify molecules as calm English narration follows the reactions. Acetyl-CoA supplies a two-carbon acetyl group to four-carbon oxaloacetate, forming six-carbon citrate; CoA-SH is released.

Citrate rearranges into six-carbon isocitrate. Isocitrate becomes five-carbon α-ketoglutarate: CO₂ leaves and the first NADH appears. Next, four-carbon succinyl-CoA forms, releasing a second CO₂ and producing a second NADH. The departing carbons are not the newly arrived acetyl carbons.

Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate, releasing CoA-SH; a GTP → ATP callout represents one ATP equivalent, not two additional products. Membrane-embedded succinate dehydrogenase converts succinate to fumarate as FAD becomes FADH₂. Water enters as fumarate becomes malate.

Malate becomes oxaloacetate, producing the third NADH. The regenerated oxaloacetate can accept another acetyl group, closing the loop. The completed turn shows two CO₂, three NADH, one FADH₂ and one ATP equivalent.
stages.note: research: Citric acid cycle — research for one complete turn inside a mitochondrion, rather than a historical discovery episode. Follow acetyl-group entry, energy capture, carbon dioxide release and oxaloacetate regeneration. Dates below identify source publication dates, not dates when these recurring biochemical reactions occurred. The 60-second running time is a presentation choice, not the measured duration of one turn.

items.prompt:
Clean 2D textbook animation in 16:9, with flat colors and crisp diagram lines.
0–4 s: One continuous view: an oval mitochondrial cutaway with double membrane and folded inner membrane surrounds a symbolic clockwise reaction loop. Above: 'Citric acid cycle'; inside: 'Matrix'. A calm adult English narrator, named Narrator, says exactly: 'In the mitochondrial matrix, the Krebs cycle begins.'
4–12 s: Reveal 'Oxaloacetate 4C' at top. 'Acetyl-CoA' enters; only its two-carbon group joins oxaloacetate. Reveal 'Citrate 6C'; 'CoA-SH' leaves. Narrator: 'Acetyl-CoA contributes two carbons to four-carbon oxaloacetate, forming citrate and releasing coenzyme A.'
12–15 s: Advance clockwise to 'Isocitrate 6C'; rearrange its schematic carbon skeleton. Narrator: 'Citrate rearranges into isocitrate.'
15–22 s: Reveal 'α-Ketoglutarate 5C'. One 'CO₂' badge leaves; one 'NADH' badge appears beside the arrow. Narrator: 'Isocitrate becomes alpha-ketoglutarate, releasing carbon dioxide and making NADH.'
22–30 s: Advance to lower-right 'Succinyl-CoA 4C'; a second 'CO₂' and second 'NADH' appear. Narrator: 'Then succinyl-CoA forms, releasing another carbon dioxide and making another NADH. Neither departing carbon is newly arrived.' Keep incoming acetyl carbons distinct and retained; only original oxaloacetate carbons leave. Hold succinyl-CoA highlighted, with the next arrow beginning to glow.
No other text, no cuts, no music, no subtitles.

Continue directly from @previous, the last frame of the previous segment: the same scene, style, people and objects, mid-action. Continue directly from the attached frame 'previous': the same scene, style, people and objects, mid-action.
Clean 2D textbook animation in 16:9, with flat colors and crisp diagram lines.
0–7 s: Continue the glowing arrow from succinyl-CoA to 'Succinate 4C'. Release 'CoA-SH'; show one callout 'GTP → ATP', not two product badges. Narrator: 'Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate, releasing coenzyme A. GTP supplies one ATP equivalent.'
7–14 s: At the adjacent inner-membrane fold, highlight a simple schematic block labeled 'Succinate dehydrogenase'. Route the reaction arrow through it to 'Fumarate 4C'; change 'FAD' to 'FADH₂'. This block is a diagram symbol, not a molecular likeness. Narrator: 'Membrane-embedded succinate dehydrogenase forms fumarate, converting FAD to FADH2.'
14–18 s: An 'H₂O' badge enters the next arrow; reveal 'Malate 4C'. Narrator: 'Adding water makes malate.'
18–23 s: Advance to the existing oxaloacetate panel, closing the loop. Add the third 'NADH' badge. Narrator: 'Malate regenerates oxaloacetate, producing the third NADH.'
23–30 s: Pulse the closed loop once. Gather existing product badges into a clear bottom strip: 'Per turn', '2 CO₂', '3 NADH', '1 FADH₂', '1 ATP equivalent'. Replace the GTP callout with that single ATP total. Another acetyl group approaches oxaloacetate without completing another turn. Narrator: 'Oxaloacetate accepts another acetyl group. These are the totals per turn.' Hold the completed diagram and persistent title.
No other text, no cuts, no music, no subtitles.
